=== src/lib/content/crm-h.yaml
crm-h › name: SaaS CRM H
crm-h › nickname: CRM platform plus CSBC servers
crm-h › tagline: Case work and rules on the CRM platform. Money, decision records and a backup copy stay with CSBC.
crm-h › summary › 1: In this option, workers, clients and partners use the CRM platform for case work, online portals, notices and the business rules that drive process. The CRM platform is a large software-as-a-service running on the providers systems, not the CSBC's.
crm-h › summary › 2: The parts that are most critical move to CSBC's own servers. These are the payment run, the financial ledger, the evidence (documents and submissions), the record of each decision, and a live backup copy of the records. CSBC changes those parts on its own calendar, so the CRM provider's upgrade dates cannot land in the middle of the monthly payment run.
crm-h › summary › 3: This costs more than putting everything on the CRM platform. The team has to build and run the CSBC-side parts and join two platforms together. In return, if the CRM platform ever cut off access, clients could still be paid the same amount as last time. New decisions would wait until the CRM platform came back.
crm-h › facts › 1 › label: CRM-side effort (likely)
crm-h › facts › 1 › value: 750 labour-months, in a range of 474 to 1,146. Approx $34M to $53M in labour costs.
crm-h › facts › 2 › label: CSBC-side parts
crm-h › facts › 2 › value: 320 labour-months, in a range of 280 to 725. Approx $14.5M to $23M in labour costs. This scope is: financial components, evidence/document management, decision records and back-up.
crm-h › facts › 3 › label: CRM licences
crm-h › facts › 3 › value: Varies according to vendor, given market average: $44M to $80M a year at list price for about 9,400 staff, before discount. Portal logins, the integration platform and add-ons are extra and like make the discount a wash.
crm-h › facts › 4 › label: Upgrade testing
crm-h › facts › 4 › value: About 90 to 210 labour-days a year to test each of the CRM provider's three yearly upgrades.
crm-h › goodAt › 1: The monthly payment run sits on the CSBC's own servers and is changed on CSBC's own calendar.
crm-h › goodAt › 2: Each decision is copied off the CRM platform into an queryable and auditable store.
crm-h › goodAt › 3: If the CRM provider cut off access, staff can still view case snapshots, manually process new applications and repeat last month's payments.
crm-h › goodAt › 4: CSBC gets a trusted internal ledger that balances every transaction and accrual.
crm-h › goodAt › 5: Work screens, portals, and business rules capabilities come built-in with the CRM platform - but still require customization, as in the all-CRM option.
crm-h › watchOut › 1: If the CRM provider cuts off access, ordinary business processing halts - back-ups capture point in time, but regular business activity requires CRM.
crm-h › watchOut › 2: Everything within the CRM platform, including business rules, gets upgraded on CRM provider's schedule.
crm-h › watchOut › 3: The CSBC-side estimates are predicated on small licensing footprint, additional proprietary systems will drive up licensing.
crm-h › watchOut › 4: Two platforms must be joined and kept in step, which adds work and more places for things to break.
crm-h › watchOut › 5: All SaaS major CRM providers are subject to the USA CLOUD Act regardless of residency of the system and social sector data (regardless of classification) must flow through their managed Landing Zones, which are opaque to government.
crm-h › watchOut › 6: The CRM is unlikely to make effective use of the on-premise data lake being built as part of CriDIR
crm-h › watchOut › 7: The work on the MySS rebuilt would be invalidated and a rebuild within the CRM tool would be necessary
crm-h › watchOut › 8: Licences are large, recurring and complex to optimize.

crm-h › zones › 1 › blurb: The people who use the system every day: government staff, clients and the agencies and service providers who work with them.
crm-h › zones › 2 › name: Finance partners
crm-h › zones › 2 › blurb: Banks, credit unions and government financial authorities that manage payment distribution.
crm-h › zones › 3 › name: SaaS CRM platform
crm-h › zones › 3 › blurb: The part run by the CRM provider on its own computers: the screens, the case work, the rules and the notices.
crm-h › zones › 3 › groups › 1 › name: Experience
crm-h › zones › 3 › groups › 2 › name: Case work
crm-h › zones › 3 › groups › 3 › name: Services in the CRM platform
crm-h › zones › 4 › name: Integration platform, on CSBC servers
crm-h › zones › 4 › blurb: Connecting software, bought from the CRM provider but run on CSBC's own servers, that carries information between the CRM platform and everything else.
crm-h › zones › 5 › name: The CSBC's own servers
crm-h › zones › 5 › blurb: The parts the CSBC runs itself and changes on its own calendar: money, decision records, evidence and the backup copy.
crm-h › zones › 5 › groups › 1 › name: Money
crm-h › zones › 5 › groups › 2 › name: Decisions and evidence
crm-h › zones › 5 › groups › 3 › name: Events and backup
crm-h › zones › 6 › name: Partner systems
crm-h › zones › 6 › blurb: Social sector partners that help deliver services, or whose information contributes to a connected service experience.
crm-h › components › workers › name: Workers
crm-h › components › workers › short: About 9,400 government staff
crm-h › components › workers › what: Employment assistance workers, aseworkers, supervisors, intake staff etc.
crm-h › components › workers › does: They take applications, check eligibility, plan services, and approve payments. They do almost all of this in CRM screens.
crm-h › components › workers › why: Staff spend their whole working day in this system. How well it works decides how fast clients get help and how much time gets wasted in process.
crm-h › components › clients › name: Clients and representatives
crm-h › components › clients › short: People applying for or getting help
crm-h › components › clients › what: People who apply for employment assistance or disability assistance, youth and families, and anyone acting for them.
crm-h › components › clients › does: They apply, send monthly reports, ask for supplements, ask for a decision to be looked at again and upload documents through online portals.
crm-h › components › clients › why: Clients depend on the money and services arriving on time. A system they can use on their own saves them trips, time and phone calls.
crm-h › components › partners › name: Partners
crm-h › components › partners › short: Agencies, caregivers and youth
crm-h › components › partners › what: Delegated and contracted agencies, Indigenous authorities, foster caregivers and youth in care.
crm-h › components › partners › does: They see and update the parts of a case they are allowed to, through their own portals.
crm-h › components › partners › why: Much of child protection work is done by partners. They need the right information, and only the right information, to keep children safe.
crm-h › components › finance › name: Finance partners
crm-h › components › finance › short: Bank, BC Mail Plus, government accounting, Treasury
crm-h › components › finance › what: The bank, the print vendor BC Mail Plus, the government's corporate accounting system and Provincial Treasury.
crm-h › components › finance › does: They receive the payment files for direct deposits and cheques. They send back what was paid, returned or rejected so it can be matched up.
crm-h › components › finance › why: This is where money actually reaches clients. Every file must be right, on time and checked against what the bank says it paid.
crm-h › components › console › name: Worker screens
crm-h › components › console › short: Staff screens, routing and phone line
crm-h › components › console › what: The main screen staff work in, built from the CRM platform's standard tools. It includes work queues and the phone system for the reporting line.
crm-h › components › console › does: It shows each worker their cases and tasks, sends new work to the right person and lets supervisors watch the workload. Reporting-line calls come straight into the case.
crm-h › components › console › why: A clear console means less time hunting for information and fewer missed tasks. Its look and its upgrade dates are set by the CRM provider, not the ministry.
crm-h › components › console › buildBuy › label: Buy: CRM licence for each staff member
crm-h › components › console › buildBuy › summary: The console comes bundled with most CRM providers', licensed per staff member. The phone feature is typically a separate per-user licence.
crm-h › components › console › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Phone bank console
crm-h › components › console › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Included in the per-user licence.
crm-h › components › console › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: VoIP add-on for the service desk product
crm-h › components › console › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: For reporting-line calls. Extra per-user licence plus phone charges.
crm-h › components › console › watch › text: The CRM provider upgrades this three times a year on its own dates. CSBC cannot pause those upgrades.
crm-h › components › portals › name: Online portals
crm-h › components › portals › short: Websites for clients and partners
crm-h › components › portals › what: Websites built on the CRM platform for clients, representatives, youth, caregivers and partner agencies.
crm-h › components › portals › does: Clients apply, send monthly reports and request supplements. Partners see their share of a case. Guided forms walk people through each step.
crm-h › components › portals › why: Good portals cut phone calls and office visits. They also cut retyping by staff, which is where errors creep in.
crm-h › components › portals › buildBuy › label: Buy: the CRM portal product
crm-h › components › portals › buildBuy › summary: Portals use the CRM portal product, licensed per member or per login. CSBC has numerous CRM portals today.
crm-h › components › portals › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: CRM portal product
crm-h › components › portals › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Priced per member or per login, on top of staff licences.
crm-h › components › portals › watch › text: Portals are on the CRM provider's upgrade dates and stop if the CRM provider cuts off access.
crm-h › components › case-work › name: Case work
crm-h › components › case-work › short: Applications, case plans, deadlines, approvals
crm-h › components › case-work › what: The heart of the system, built on the CRM provider's SaaS product. Typically the product is broken up into packages, one per service category.
crm-h › components › case-work › does: It handles intake, case plans, court steps, work lists and legal deadlines. It also checks that a worker has the authority to make a decision on that date.
crm-h › components › case-work › why: This is where most of the building happens. No product comes prepackaged to model acts and regulations, bespoke business processes or domain specific rules, so the rules, deadlines and approval checks are custom work on any product.
crm-h › components › case-work › buildBuy › label: Buy: the CRM provider's package, then configure
crm-h › components › case-work › buildBuy › summary: The CRM provider supplies generic record containers for benefits, care plans, providers and court steps. BC's specific policies and rules are built on top.
crm-h › components › case-work › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: CRM package
crm-h › components › case-work › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Basic records and workflow. BC-specific work is built on top. The closer the CRM default is to existing models, the less customization work is needed.
crm-h › components › case-work › watch › text: All programs share a single CRM, so they cannot be changed and released fully on their ownk, and program-level customizations are very limited.
crm-h › components › rules › name: Rules
crm-h › components › rules › short: Works out eligibility and amounts
crm-h › components › rules › what: The CRM provider's rules engine. It holds every processing and evaluation rule, including eligibility, how much they get, with the date each rule starts.
crm-h › components › rules › does: It works out elements like eligibility and payment amounts and explains how it got there. Each result, with its inputs and the rule version used, is sent off the CRM platform as the record of the decision.
crm-h › components › rules › why: Policy determines eligibility and entitlements deterministically - once the relevant facts are established, there is no room for human judgement. Workers evaluate claims and the submitted evidence and make determinations as to the sufficiency of this evidence. A rules engine ensures administrative fairness, improves processing speed and reliability, and enhances traceability and auditability.
crm-h › components › rules › buildBuy › label: Platform: part of the CRM licence
crm-h › components › rules › buildBuy › summary: Most CRM vendors include some sort of business rules component or an integration with a common commercial tool (e.g. Camunda).
crm-h › components › rules › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: CRM rules engine
crm-h › components › rules › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Included. Monthly usage limit not confirmed by the CRM provider.
crm-h › components › rules › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Separate rules service on CSBC servers
crm-h › components › rules › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: Earlier projects developed a business rules management system, this could be quickly refactored for use.
crm-h › components › rules › watch › text: If the CRM provider cuts off access both the rules system and its inputs become unavailable. A self-hosted rules engine still depends on data collected by and held in the CRM.
crm-h › components › notices › name: Notices and documents
crm-h › components › notices › short: Letters, forms and court papers
crm-h › components › notices › what: Most CRM systems offer a document generator and management mechanism for letters, notifications etc.
crm-h › components › notices › does: It produces each notice and keeps the finished copy as the record of what was sent. There are currently over 1,200 such documents or forms managed today.
crm-h › components › notices › why: Document management is a significant portion of the labour effort in ICM today for both business and IT staff. Even small efficiencies here will pay dividends.
crm-h › components › notices › buildBuy › label: Platform: part of the CRM licence
crm-h › components › notices › buildBuy › summary: Document creation is typically included with the CRM SaaS product, or an integration an integration with a leading commercial product (e.g. Adobe Experience Manager) is also available. Most CRM providers do not include an e-signature product - as this is not a requirement of any business process, it can be excluded.
crm-h › components › notices › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: CRM document generation
crm-h › components › notices › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Typically included, where it is not, license with integrated provider is next-best alternative.
crm-h › components › notices › watch › text: Many CRM systems impose limits on the throughput of documents and have steep overage charges - or fractionally less steep subscriptions.
crm-h › components › platform-services › name: Platform services
crm-h › components › platform-services › short: Security, privacy, backup add-ons
crm-h › components › platform-services › what: Most CRMs have a long list of security, logging, instrumentation, privacy protection, encryption, and back-up addons. These are often ignored or excluded from initial estimates. Additional add-ons include personal data request management, data redaction features, etc. Many CRM SaaS providers delegate these features to the extension marketplace.
crm-h › components › platform-services › does: They encrypt data, watch who opens what, keep field history for up to 10 years, and apply retention and deletion rules.
crm-h › components › platform-services › why: Client and child protection records are among the most sensitive the province holds. These add-ons are how the CRM provider protects them and proves who saw them.
crm-h › components › platform-services › buildBuy › label: Buy: CRM add-ons
crm-h › components › platform-services › buildBuy › summary: Each is a separate CRM product whose cost typically scales with the total size of the CRM rather than usage of the specific tool.
crm-h › components › platform-services › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Security add-on
crm-h › components › platform-services › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Encryption, access monitoring, field history.
crm-h › components › platform-services › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Privacy add-on
crm-h › components › platform-services › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: Retention, deletion and privacy requests.

crm-h › components › platform-services › buildBuy › options › 3 › note: Hides personal data in test copies.
crm-h › components › platform-services › buildBuy › options › 4 › name: Backup add-on
crm-h › components › platform-services › buildBuy › options › 4 › note: Backup and restore.
crm-h › components › platform-services › watch › text: By default, CRM SaaS products use a single site-wide encryption key - so crypto-shredding is impossible.
crm-h › components › open-host › name: Service API
crm-h › components › open-host › short: One agreed way in and out
crm-h › components › open-host › what: A single API for other systems to talk to the case system, using the business's own words for things. It runs on the integration platform on CSBC servers.
crm-h › components › open-host › does: It brings decision records, evidence and payment requests out of the CRM platform to the CSBC-side parts. It sends payment status back in.
crm-h › components › open-host › why: Other systems connect to this API, not to the CRM platform's inner workings.
crm-h › components › open-host › buildBuy › label: Buy: the integration platform, run on CSBC servers
crm-h › components › open-host › buildBuy › summary: Most CRM providers have a standard integration solution - either as a subsidiary or as a de facto standard. This integration tool runs within CSBC servers. In most cases, licensing is either free (where open source) or a combination of capacity and consumption.
crm-h › components › open-host › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Integration platform
crm-h › components › open-host › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Run on CSBC servers, with the gateway managed by CSBC.
crm-h › components › change-relay › name: Change feed
crm-h › components › change-relay › short: Sends every CRM change out
crm-h › components › change-relay › what: A feed that notices each change to records in the CRM platform and passes it on.
crm-h › components › change-relay › does: It passes changes to the event stream on CSBC servers. From there they reach the backup copy and the analysis store.
crm-h › components › change-relay › why: This is what keeps CSBC's backup copy current. Without it the backup would be out of date when it is needed most.
crm-h › components › change-relay › buildBuy › label: Buy: CRM add-on, carried by the integration platform
crm-h › components › change-relay › buildBuy › summary: Most CRMs providers have a very basic built-in change-feed and sell a change-feed add-on or subscription with more data, higher limits. They are typically priced with a flat-fee plus a usage rate. The integration platform carries the changes to CSBC's servers.
crm-h › components › change-relay › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: CRM platform events and change data capture add-on
crm-h › components › change-relay › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Most CRM providers have a low default limit, which must be raised through payment.
crm-h › components › change-relay › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Integration platform
crm-h › components › change-relay › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: Carries the feed to CSBC servers.
crm-h › components › change-relay › watch › text: Most CRM platforms do not support durable event logs - with change feeds lasting a few days. If connectivity to the change feed is lost for long periods, desyncronization between systems is possible, recovery is difficult and manual.
crm-h › components › secure-exchange › name: APS P2P
crm-h › components › secure-exchange › short: A secure data exchange among government organizations
crm-h › components › secure-exchange › what: The connection to the province's APS P2P, this is an end-point for the integration platform.
crm-h › components › secure-exchange › does: It provides a security server to enable connectivity to the APS P2P network for connected data.
crm-h › components › secure-exchange › why: To ensure secure, privacy respecting and transparent data usage. A log of each exchange shows what data was shared, with whom and when.
crm-h › components › secure-exchange › buildBuy › label: Utilize the existing APS P2P platform security server pattern.
crm-h › components › secure-exchange › buildBuy › summary: The CRM product cannot host the security server itself, so the integration platform acts as the conduit - both client and server to the connected service network.
crm-h › components › secure-exchange › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: APS P2P
crm-h › components › secure-exchange › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Uses the APS P2P common component.
crm-h › components › financial-components › name: Financial components
crm-h › components › financial-components › short: Debts, recovery and payment amounts
crm-h › components › financial-components › what: The CSBC-built module that turns decisions and actions into accrual accounting events and transactions. It ocvers overpayments, repayable amounts, and can be expanded to capture flexible payment schedules and types.
crm-h › components › financial-components › does: It converts decisions made into accrual accounting events, works out overpayments, underpayments, receivables, establishes repayment plans, etc. It maintains the authoritative ledger and reconciles accounts based on transaction records return by payment providers.
crm-h › components › financial-components › why: The current financial calculations and processings are embedded entirely within the mainframe system. Managing the many edge-cases and regular irregularities of payments gracefully would bring tremendous productivity yields.
crm-h › components › financial-components › buildBuy › label: Build: on the CSBC's own servers
crm-h › components › financial-components › buildBuy › summary: Four successive research projects starting in 2022 through to 2026 have compared dozens of financial products. The recommendation of each such analysis was the same - build. This recommendation holds.
crm-h › components › financial-components › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Build
crm-h › components › financial-components › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Recommended direction.
crm-h › components › financial-components › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Apache Fineract
crm-h › components › financial-components › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: Top score, but brings its own client and loan model.
crm-h › components › financial-components › watch › text: Pulling financial processing out of the CRM ensures total control over the highest risk component and prevents disruption caused by CRM updates.
crm-h › components › ledger › name: Ledger
crm-h › components › ledger › short: The money record, balanced every day
crm-h › components › ledger › what: The ledger is the authoritative account maintained by the financial components. It is compliant with established standards and ensures a rigorous, immutable log of all financial activity is kept and recoverable. Here it is an append-only table in a CSBC-managed database.
crm-h › components › ledger › does: It records every payment and recovery as balanced entries that can never be changed. It is checked against the bank and the government's accounts every day.
crm-h › components › ledger › why: Reconciliation is a scattershot and largely manual process today.
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › label: Build: a locked table in CSBC's database
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › summary: A test compared a plain table in the free PostgreSQL database with three leading ledger engines: TigerBeetle, Formance Ledger and Blnk Core. The plain table passed all nine tests and no engine did better, so the proposed direction is to build. TigerBeetle is the one to revisit if volumes outgrow one database.
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Table in PostgreSQL
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Recommended. Passed all nine tests; one test run only.
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: TigerBeetle
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: Fast, but needs a second store for details. Revisit if volumes grow.
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › options › 3 › name: Formance Ledger
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › options › 3 › note: Allowed details to be rewritten; kept deleted values.
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › options › 4 › name: Blnk Core
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › options › 4 › note: Allowed details to be rewritten; needs extra moving parts.
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › options › 5 › name: Apache Fineract
crm-h › components › ledger › buildBuy › options › 5 › note: Brings its own client and loan model.
crm-h › components › ledger › watch › text: The CRM-S route lacks a true ledger - which is a crucial element of financial management that costs the province thousands of labour-hours and millions of dollars.
crm-h › components › payments › name: Payments and benefit issuance
crm-h › components › payments › short: The monthly payment run
crm-h › components › payments › what: The one place payments leave CSBC. It runs on CSBC servers and makes the direct deposit and cheque files.
crm-h › components › payments › does: It turns approved payment requests into files for the bank, BC Mail Plus and government accounts. It records what was paid, returned or rejected.
crm-h › components › payments › why: The volume of low-value payments issued by the social sector vastly outstrips the processing capabilities and transaction limits of common government providers like CFS. Instead, all payment processing is currently handled by MIS, and this will be taken up in the modern system by a dedicated component. The sensitivity of this component is such that it must run on CSBC's servers.
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › label: Build: on the CSBC's own servers
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › summary: Research has examined 58 commercial payment hobs and providers, as well as open-source or self-hosted commercial payment management systems. Of the 58 commercial providers, 52 were subsidiaries of foreign financial institutions (USA, China, Ukraine, Luxembourg, and Curaçao. Of the Canadian options, the transparency and logging mechanism would almost certainly fall short of government accounting standards. Thus, the proposed direction is to build, using an existing framework, a payment management utility that extends the financial components.
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Build
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Recommended direction.
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Bottomline Payments Hub
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: Top score among commercial providers.
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › options › 3 › name: Kyriba Payments
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › options › 3 › note: Next-best.
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › options › 4 › name: moov-io/cadeft
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › options › 4 › note: Library for direct deposit files; not mature.
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › options › 5 › name: Payment Hub EE and OpenG2P
crm-h › components › payments › buildBuy › options › 5 › note: Designs to learn from, not to adopt.
crm-h › components › payments › watch › text: The payment run is released on CSBC's own calendar, so it can be frozen around payment day. CRM-S cannot do this.
crm-h › components › decision-store › name: Decision record store
crm-h › components › decision-store › short: Locked record of every decision
crm-h › components › decision-store › what: A store on CSBC servers that keeps the full record of each decision. Records are linked in a chain, so any later change shows.
crm-h › components › decision-store › does: It receives each decision's inputs, the rules version used, the step-by-step working and the outcome from the CRM platform. It keeps them for as long as required.
crm-h › components › decision-store › why: When a client asks for a review or appeals, this record shows exactly what was decided and why and is instantly queryable and recoverable.
crm-h › components › decision-store › buildBuy › label: Build: on the CSBC's own servers
crm-h › components › decision-store › buildBuy › summary: There are numerous highly-specific ways this record must be stored, presented, secured, queryed and managed. No commercial product keeps decision records the way the social sector requires.
crm-h › components › decision-store › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Build
crm-h › components › decision-store › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Highest security, most ergonomic.
crm-h › components › decision-store › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Keep the record inside the CRM platform
crm-h › components › decision-store › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: CRM provider has limitless and indefinite access to every record in the system.
crm-h › components › decision-store › watch › text: Decision records are kept off the CRM platform in a chain that shows any change. Kept on the CRM, every record could captured, corrupted or tampered with at any time.
crm-h › components › rules-archive › name: Rules snapshot archive
crm-h › components › rules-archive › short: A copy of every rules version
crm-h › components › rules-archive › what: A store on CSBC servers holding an exact copy of every version of the rules, made the moment it is switched on.
crm-h › components › rules-archive › does: Each copy gets a fingerprint. Each decision record carries the fingerprint of the rules it used.
crm-h › components › rules-archive › why: Years later, anyone can see the exact rule that applied to a client's decision. It does not matter whether the CRM platform still has it.
crm-h › components › rules-archive › buildBuy › label: Build: on the CSBC's own servers
crm-h › components › rules-archive › buildBuy › summary: The rules are exported from the CRM platform when each version is switched on and stored here. This is new work for this option.
crm-h › components › rules-archive › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Build
crm-h › components › rules-archive › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Export, fingerprint and store each rules version.
crm-h › components › rules-archive › watch › text: The copies are evidence only. They cannot run outside the CRM platform to make new decisions.
crm-h › components › drift-check › name: Drift check
crm-h › components › drift-check › short: Catches rules changed in place
crm-h › components › drift-check › what: A scheduled check that validates the rule base for currency, correctness and coherence.
crm-h › components › drift-check › does: If there are issues with the rule base, it is rolled back to the last valid state and notifications raised.
crm-h › components › drift-check › why: Business rules changes (such as rate changes) can go-live accidentally, or changes can conflict with existing rules inadvertantly. This check ensures that rules changes never break the rule set and never go live accidentally.
crm-h › components › drift-check › buildBuy › label: Build: a scheduled check
crm-h › components › drift-check › buildBuy › summary: No reviewed CRM provider includes integrity or coherence checks as part of the rules platform - these would need to be developed.
crm-h › components › drift-check › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Build
crm-h › components › drift-check › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Can be added to the rules archive
crm-h › components › drift-check › watch › text: It cannot actively block bad updates - administrators must remember to test the draft ruleset before deploying.
crm-h › components › evidence-store › name: Evidence and verification store
crm-h › components › evidence-store › short: Permanent record of claims, evidence and determinations.
crm-h › components › evidence-store › what: A store on CSBC servers that keeps every claim a client made, the evidence they provided to corroborate it, and the determination made by the worker about that claim. This record is immutable and append-only.
crm-h › components › evidence-store › does: It keeps a chronology of all submissions, assertions, evidence and facts, including corrections, redactions, and rescindments. It holds this for the full retention period.
crm-h › components › evidence-store › why: Evidence and claims are the constituent element of a client's submission, determinations are space for judgment on the part of the worker. Decision reviews, audits and tribunals are only as effective as the quality of the evidence they can review. A full history makes such review work straightforward.
crm-h › components › evidence-store › buildBuy › label: Build: on the event stream
crm-h › components › evidence-store › buildBuy › summary: Three rounds of research (2023, 2024, 2026) found no commercial product or mature open source project that captures the evidence record in a workable fashion. The recommendation is to adopt an open source event broker, and build the evidence store using that.
crm-h › components › evidence-store › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Build on Apache Kafka
crm-h › components › evidence-store › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Recommended direction.
crm-h › components › evidence-store › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Evidence kept in the CRM platform
crm-h › components › evidence-store › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: CRMs charge for storage usage and transfer bandwidth - evidence records typically include binary files like scanned documents or PDF documents. CRM providers cannot be reasonably expected to comply with the retention periods contemplated by CFD. CRM providers do not have the forensic capabilities to make this capability fully mature.
crm-h › components › evidence-store › watch › text: Fact records are maintained off the CRM platform as the permanent, immutable and authoritative history. The CRM records are an ephemeral "working copy"
crm-h › components › kafka › name: Event stream (Kafka)
crm-h › components › kafka › short: Carries every change, in order
crm-h › components › kafka › what: Kafka is free software that works like a conveyor belt for events. Each change or decision goes on in order and stays there for as long as needed. A registry checks every event has the agreed shape.
crm-h › components › kafka › does: It carries changes from the CRM platform to the evidence store, backup copy and analysis store. Any part can replay past messages to rebuild its records.
crm-h › components › kafka › why: The CRM platform's own messages vanish after 72 hours. This stream keeps them, so a part that falls behind can catch up without losing anything, and system behaviour can be monitored effectively. Event-driven orchestration of services is the most sustainable and scalable way to offer a "ask once" connected service experience.
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › label: Open source: Apache Kafka, run by CSBC
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › summary: The recommendation is to either adopt Apache Kafka has a corporate common component (an enterprise needs only one Kafka instance), or barring that, use a light-weight event broker such as Red Panda or NATS.
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Apache Kafka common component
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Recommended.
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Apicurio Registry or Karapace
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: Free schema registries
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › options › 3 › name: Confluent or Redpanda
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › options › 3 › note: Recommended only if use is limited to social sector.
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › options › 4 › name: NATS, Polars
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › options › 4 › note: Lighter-weight alternatives to Kafka, recommended only if use is limited to social sector.
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › options › 5 › name: CRM event bus
crm-h › components › kafka › buildBuy › options › 5 › note: Keeps messages only 72 hours.
crm-h › components › kafka › watch › text: Changes can be replayed long after 72 hours, in order. CRM-S cannot do this.
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › name: Continuity copy
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › short: Live backup of the records
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › what: A copy of the case records kept on CSBC servers. It is updated all the time while the CRM platform is running.
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › does: It keeps the records current, so the fallback applications can run from it if the CRM platform is cut off.
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › why: If the supplier ever cut off access, the ministry would still have its records.
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › buildBuy › label: Build: on CSBC's own servers
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › buildBuy › summary: CSBC requires a live, on-premise copy for any core product run by a supplier. The CRM platform's change feed fills it. The copy itself is built and run by CSBC.
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Build, fed by the change feed
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Required by the programme's continuity direction.
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Scheduled export
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: The all-CRM way. Older data, not a live copy.
crm-h › components › continuity-copy › watch › text: The records stay current on CSBC servers if the CRM platform is cut off.
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › name: Fallback applications
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › short: Keep going if the CRM platform is cut off
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › what: Small applications on CSBC servers that run from the continuity copy.
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › does: They let staff view cases and take new applications. They also run a payment that repeats last month's amounts through the same ledger checks.
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › why: Clients would still be paid if the supplier cut off access. They would get the same amount as last time until the CRM platform came back.
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › buildBuy › label: Build: on CSBC's own servers
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › buildBuy › summary: The team builds a case viewer, intake and a repeat-payment run. No business area has yet said it needs more than repeating last month's payments.
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Build
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Case viewer, intake and repeat payments.
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Manual emergency payments
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: The all-CRM way, carried over from today's plan.
crm-h › components › fallback-apps › watch › text: Payments can repeat last month's amounts if the CRM platform is cut off. New decisions and changes in amount would wait.
crm-h › components › lakehouse › name: Analysis store
crm-h › components › lakehouse › short: Reports without extra copies
crm-h › components › lakehouse › what: A store on CSBC servers for reports and analysis, fed from the event stream.
crm-h › components › lakehouse › does: It lets analysts and managers report on caseloads, payments and outcomes from the same records the system uses.
crm-h › components › lakehouse › why: Today reporting relies on a separate copy of the data. Each extra copy is another place personal information can leak or go out of date.
crm-h › components › reporting-line › name: Emergency & Reporting-line Backup Path
crm-h › components › reporting-line › short: Emergency & Child protection calls during outages
crm-h › components › reporting-line › what: A simple intake path on CSBC servers for emergency requests and the 24-hour child protection reporting line.
crm-h › components › reporting-line › does: It lets staff respond to a subset of issues and record reports of a child at risk when the CRM platform is unavailable. The reports are correlated with their case files when connectivity is re-established.
crm-h › components › reporting-line › why: The director must receive and assess every report, day or night. CRM maintenance often falls at nights and weekends, when these lines are busiest.
crm-h › components › reporting-line › buildBuy › label: Build: on CSBC's own servers
crm-h › components › reporting-line › buildBuy › summary: The CRM provider cannot exempt one part of the system from its maintenance. A small separate path is built instead.
crm-h › components › reporting-line › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Build
crm-h › components › reporting-line › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: A small intake path off the CRM platform.
crm-h › components › reporting-line › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Paper or offline capture
crm-h › components › reporting-line › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: Back-entered later.
crm-h › components › reporting-line › watch › text: Only a basic intake path. The full reporting-line screens still follow the CRM provider's maintenance dates.
crm-h › components › government › name: Government and justice partners
crm-h › components › government › short: Canada Revenue Agency, courts, police and others
crm-h › components › government › what: Partners such as the Canada Revenue Agency, Service Canada, courts, police, Vital Statistics, Pacific Blue Cross and Indigenous authorities.
crm-h › components › government › does: They send and receive information, such as income checks and court orders, through the integration platform.
crm-h › components › government › why: Many decisions rely on facts from these partners. Getting the information quickly and safely means fewer delays and fewer errors for clients.

=== src/lib/content/crm-s.yaml
crm-s › name: SaaS CRM S
crm-s › nickname: All on the CRM platform
crm-s › tagline: Every part of the new system runs on the CRM platform, set up to work the way ICM works today.
crm-s › summary › 1: In this option, the CRM platform replaces Siebel, the rules engine, the mainframe payment system and the monthly cheque run. Case work, applications, rules, notices, payments and the online portals all live in one CRM system. Rules, payments and history keep the shape they have today.
crm-s › summary › 2: Prototyping and research has found that a replacement of ICM can technically be built this way, but the trade-offs are significant. Roughly a quarter of the total business capabilities required are included "out of the box" with the remainder being custom work built inside the SaaS platform. None of this is impossible as a whole - but the improvements over the current ICM mechanisms are largely cosmetic and performance - the constraints are only marginally less confining that in ICM.
crm-s › summary › 3: Beyond the technical complexity, the biggest catch is control. The CRM provider, not government, decides how the platform behaves, when it changes, and whether it runs at all. Moreover, all data must go through infrastructure wholly out of sight of government. Beyond that, there are several compromises business will have to agree to in order to make adoption workable.
crm-s › facts › 1 › label: Likely build effort
crm-s › facts › 1 › value: 646 labour-months
crm-s › facts › 2 › label: Effort range
crm-s › facts › 2 › value: 415 to 998 labour-months
crm-s › facts › 3 › label: Staff licenses given average posted prices
crm-s › facts › 3 › value: About $44M to $80M a year, before discount and add-ons
crm-s › facts › 4 › label: Requirements met by setup alone
crm-s › facts › 4 › value: 107 of 481 (22%)
crm-s › goodAt › 1: It is the lowest-effort way to build the system on the CRM platform.
crm-s › goodAt › 2: Rules become dated versions in one place, instead of old and new rule sets kept side by side.
crm-s › goodAt › 3: Sealed records become possible. ICM has no way to seal a record today.
crm-s › goodAt › 4: Overpayment amounts are worked out in the system, not printed, scanned and typed into the mainframe again.
crm-s › goodAt › 5: There is familiarity within CSBC with several leading commercial CRM providers
crm-s › watchOut › 1: The CRM provider sets its own upgrade dates. CSBC cannot freeze change around the monthly cheque run, which it can do today.
crm-s › watchOut › 2: If the CRM provider cuts off access, no rules or screens can run anywhere else. Staff fall back to a manual procedures.
crm-s › watchOut › 3: Most CRM providers do not make guarantees as to data recoverability, and typically offer SLOs with credit
crm-s › watchOut › 4: Licences cost tens of millions of dollars a year at list price, every year, on top of the build.
crm-s › watchOut › 5: The investment in the Data Lake and CriDIR would be discarded.
crm-s › watchOut › 6: Any progress in MySS rebuild work would be discarded
crm-s › watchOut › 7: In all but some CRM providers, administrative users often wield nearly unlimited permissions with potentially untraceable actions. Many actions cannot be strictly forbidden, only caught after the fact.
crm-s › zones › 1 › name: People and partners
crm-s › zones › 1 › blurb: The people who use the system: ministry staff, clients and the partners who work with them.
crm-s › zones › 2 › name: SaaS CRM platform
crm-s › zones › 2 › blurb: One CRM system holds the screens, the case work for each program family and the services they share.
crm-s › zones › 2 › groups › 1 › name: Experience
crm-s › zones › 2 › groups › 2 › name: Case work, one package per program family
crm-s › zones › 2 › groups › 3 › name: Shared services
crm-s › zones › 3 › name: Integration platform, on CSBC servers
crm-s › zones › 3 › blurb: The integration platform is the CRM provider's product that connects the new system to banks, other governments and old systems. It runs on CSBC servers.
crm-s › zones › 4 › name: Outside organizations
crm-s › zones › 4 › blurb: Banks, payment partners and other governments that send or receive information.
crm-s › zones › 5 › name: The CSBC's own servers
crm-s › zones › 5 › blurb: A few pieces stay on the CSBC's own servers: reports, a backup copy of records, the emergency payment plan and Siebel until it is switched off.
crm-s › components › workers › name: Workers
crm-s › components › workers › short: About 9,400 ministry staff
crm-s › components › workers › what: The ministry staff who use the system every day. That includes employment assistance and disability workers, CFD social workers, supervisors and finance staff.
crm-s › components › workers › does: They take applications, assess need, record evidence, make decisions, issue notices and approve payments.
crm-s › components › workers › why: Each staff account needs a CRM licence. With about 9,400 accounts, staff numbers drive most of the yearly licence cost.
crm-s › components › clients › name: Clients and representatives
crm-s › components › clients › short: Applications, reports and requests
crm-s › components › clients › what: People who apply for or receive assistance, and those who act for them.
crm-s › components › clients › does: They apply, send monthly reports, ask for supplements and ask for a decision to be reviewed, mostly through the online portals.
crm-s › components › clients › why: If the system is down or slow, clients cannot report or apply. Their payments and services depend on it.
crm-s › components › partners › name: Partners
crm-s › components › partners › short: Indigenous authorities, agencies, caregivers, youth
crm-s › components › partners › what: Organizations and people who share the work with the ministry. These include Indigenous authorities, delegated and contracted agencies, caregivers, youth and other parties to a case.
crm-s › components › partners › does: They see and update the parts of a case they are allowed to, through their own portals.
crm-s › components › partners › why: Partners need the right information on time. They must also never see records they have no right to see.
crm-s › components › console › name: Worker screens
crm-s › components › console › short: Where staff do their daily work
crm-s › components › console › what: The main screens ministry staff use, built on the CRM service console. It includes the phone system for the child protection reporting line.
crm-s › components › console › does: It shows each worker their cases and tasks, routes new work to the right queue, and lets supervisors watch workloads.
crm-s › components › console › why: This is where staff spend their day. Clear screens save time and cut errors on cases that affect people's income and safety.
crm-s › components › console › buildBuy › label: Buy: CRM licence for each staff account
crm-s › components › console › buildBuy › summary: The screens come from the public sector package and the service desk product. The research priced them at US$275 to $500 per user per month at list price. Not every account may need the full licence, and no quote was sought.
crm-s › components › console › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Public sector package with the service desk product
crm-s › components › console › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Case screens, routing and supervision
crm-s › components › console › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Phone add-on for the service desk product
crm-s › components › console › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: Phone calls for the reporting line, priced per user plus phone costs
crm-s › components › console › watch › text: The 24/7 child protection reporting line runs on the same system as everything else. The CRM provider picks the maintenance and upgrade times for all of it. The line cannot get its own change window. That is not met today either.
crm-s › components › portals › name: Online portals
crm-s › components › portals › short: Online services for clients and partners
crm-s › components › portals › what: Websites where clients, representatives, youth, caregivers and partner agencies sign in. They are built with the CRM portal product.
crm-s › components › portals › does: Clients apply, send monthly reports, ask for supplements and ask for reviews. Partners work on their share of a case. The public can make reports.
crm-s › components › portals › why: Good portals mean fewer phone calls and office visits. Sign-in uses the province's own login services, so people do not need another password.
crm-s › components › portals › buildBuy › label: Buy: the CRM portal product, priced per member or per login
crm-s › components › portals › buildBuy › summary: The CRM portal product is a separate licence from the staff licence. The forms inside are built with the CRM's form tools, which come with the public sector package. The ministry already runs some CRM portals today.
crm-s › components › portals › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: CRM portal product
crm-s › components › portals › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Client, partner and public sites
crm-s › components › portals › buildBuy › options › 2 › name: Existing CRM portals
crm-s › components › portals › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: Some current ministry portals already run on a commercial CRM platform
crm-s › components › field-service › name: Field service
crm-s › components › field-service › short: Mobile work, even offline
crm-s › components › field-service › what: The CRM mobile tool for staff who work away from the office.
crm-s › components › field-service › does: It lets workers record visits in remote areas, even with no signal, and sends the notes in when they reconnect.
crm-s › components › field-service › why: Social workers visit homes far from cell coverage. They need to record what they saw at the time, not days later.
crm-s › components › field-service › buildBuy › label: Buy: the CRM field service add-on, priced per user
crm-s › components › field-service › buildBuy › summary: The field service add-on is a separate licence for the staff who need it. It is not part of the basic staff licence.
crm-s › components › adult › name: Adult assistance and disability
crm-s › components › adult › short: Employment and disability assistance cases
crm-s › components › adult › what: The case work for employment assistance and disability assistance. It is one package of custom work inside the CRM platform.
crm-s › components › adult › does: It handles applications, eligibility, monthly reports, supplements, overpayments, reviews and appeals.
crm-s › components › adult › why: These cases decide whether people get paid each month. Of 103 requirements here, 26 are met by setup alone and 56 need custom work.
crm-s › components › adult › buildBuy › label: Build on the CRM platform, using parts of the public sector package
crm-s › components › adult › buildBuy › summary: No CRM product models BC assistance law, so most of this is custom. The public sector package gives a starting data model for benefits, payments and assessments. Likely effort is about 5,570 person-days.
crm-s › components › adult › watch › text: All program families share one CRM system and one data model. They cannot be changed or upgraded on their own timetables. ICM has the same problem today.
crm-s › components › child-protection › name: Child protection and care
crm-s › components › child-protection › short: Reports, investigations, care, court
crm-s › components › child-protection › what: The case work for child protection, guardianship, children in care and caregivers. It is custom work inside the CRM platform.
crm-s › components › child-protection › does: It records reports and investigations, safety assessments, court orders, care plans and Indigenous jurisdiction steps.
crm-s › components › child-protection › why: Children's safety depends on this work being recorded correctly and on time. BC child protection law needs custom work on any product, not only the CRM platform.
crm-s › components › child-protection › buildBuy › label: Build on the CRM platform, using parts of the public sector package
crm-s › components › child-protection › buildBuy › summary: The public sector package gives building blocks for care plans, assessments, provider management and court proceedings. The rules, deadlines and Indigenous jurisdiction steps are custom.
crm-s › components › child-protection › watch › text: CRM maintenance happens at night and on weekends, when the reporting line is busiest. During those windows the system can be read-only, so staff may have to write reports down and enter them later.
crm-s › components › adoption › name: Adoption
crm-s › components › adoption › short: Adoption and post-adoption support
crm-s › components › adoption › what: The case work for adoption, including the adoption registry and post-adoption help. It is the largest single children's package.
crm-s › components › adoption › does: It tracks adoption plans, placements, post-adoption assistance and online applications.
crm-s › components › adoption › why: Adoption records must be kept for decades and some must be removed on demand by law. Likely effort is 760 person-days.
crm-s › components › adoption › buildBuy › label: Build on the CRM platform, using parts of the public sector package
crm-s › components › adoption › buildBuy › summary: Benefit and care plan parts in the public sector package cover some of the work. BC adoption steps are custom.
crm-s › components › support-needs › name: Support needs and early years
crm-s › components › support-needs › short: Children and youth with support needs
crm-s › components › support-needs › what: The case work for children and youth with support needs, and early years services.
crm-s › components › support-needs › does: It handles applications, eligibility, assessments, support plans and funding such as autism funding.
crm-s › components › support-needs › why: Families rely on this funding. The ministry's current support needs portal already runs on the CRM platform.
crm-s › components › support-needs › buildBuy › label: Build on the CRM platform, mostly by setup
crm-s › components › support-needs › buildBuy › summary: Much of this fits the public sector package's benefit management with little custom code. Likely effort is about 260 person-days.
crm-s › components › support-needs › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Existing support needs portal
crm-s › components › support-needs › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Already a CRM partner portal
crm-s › components › conditional-four › name: Four more services, if in scope
crm-s › components › conditional-four › short: Only if the ministry adds them
crm-s › components › conditional-four › what: Four services that are not in ICM today: child and youth mental health, integrated child and youth teams, and youth justice in the community and in custody.
crm-s › components › conditional-four › does: If brought into scope, they would hold clinical records, care teams, funding requests and custody records.
crm-s › components › conditional-four › why: Adding them raises effort by about 2,710 person-days. Mental health would also need the CRM provider's health product, a separate licence.
crm-s › components › conditional-four › buildBuy › label: Build on the CRM platform, if in scope
crm-s › components › conditional-four › buildBuy › summary: Mental health would use the CRM provider's health product. No CRM product runs custody centres, so the research suggests buying a custody product and connecting it.

crm-s › components › conditional-four › buildBuy › options › 3 › note: These services run on other systems today
crm-s › components › evidence › name: Evidence
crm-s › components › evidence › short: Facts about each case, with dates
crm-s › components › evidence › what: Custom CRM records that hold the facts a decision is based on, such as income, household and address.
crm-s › components › evidence › does: Each fact has the dates it was true and when it was recorded. Changes are kept in a history trail for up to 10 years, then moved to long-term storage.
crm-s › components › evidence › why: Workers, reviewers and tribunals need to know what the ministry knew when it decided. ICM today overwrites many facts.
crm-s › components › evidence › buildBuy › label: Build on the CRM platform, with field history from the security add-on
crm-s › components › evidence › buildBuy › summary: Built as custom records inside the CRM platform. Field history tracking, part of the security add-on, keeps the history of up to 60 fields per record type for 10 years.
crm-s › components › evidence › watch › text: History is kept, but records can still be edited. Corrections are marked with a label rather than kept as a separate entry. It is still better than ICM today.
crm-s › components › rules › name: Rules
crm-s › components › rules › short: Eligibility and payment rules
crm-s › components › rules › what: The rules that decide who is eligible and how much they get. They run in the CRM provider's rules engine.
crm-s › components › rules › does: It replaces the 29 rulebases in Oracle Policy Automation, the mainframe calculations, a rate table and 5 spreadsheets. Each decision keeps a record of the inputs, the rule version and the result.
crm-s › components › rules › why: One home for each rule means the same answer for the same case. Policy staff can see which version of a rule applied on a given date.
crm-s › components › rules › buildBuy › label: Platform: the rules engine, part of the public sector package
crm-s › components › rules › buildBuy › summary: Comes with the public sector package licence. Rewriting today's rules into it is about 1,180 person-days. How many rule runs the licence allows each month is unconfirmed.
crm-s › components › rules › watch › text: Each decision is fully recorded, but administrators and CRM provider staff could change that record. The record is not sealed against tampering.
crm-s › components › clocks › name: Clocks and delegation
crm-s › components › clocks › short: Deadlines and who may decide
crm-s › components › clocks › what: A custom list of every legal and policy deadline, and a check on who is allowed to use each power.
crm-s › components › clocks › does: It tracks 138 adult deadlines plus the children's time limits, counting business days and holidays. Before a director's power is used, it checks that the person had that authority on that date.
crm-s › components › clocks › why: Missed deadlines and decisions by the wrong person can harm clients and be overturned on appeal.
crm-s › components › clocks › buildBuy › label: Build on the CRM platform
crm-s › components › clocks › buildBuy › summary: The CRM platform has business hours, holidays and case milestones to build on. The deadline list and the authority check are custom work.
crm-s › components › access › name: Access and sealing
crm-s › components › access › short: Who can see which records
crm-s › components › access › what: The rules that decide which staff and partners can see which records, including sealed records.
crm-s › components › access › does: Each record gets an access class that limits who can open it. Sealed and restricted records are kept apart. The security add-on watches who looks at what and can block unusual access.
crm-s › components › access › why: Today more than a third of about 9,400 users held access they should not have had. Sealed records are new: ICM cannot seal a record.
crm-s › components › access › buildBuy › label: Build on the CRM platform, with security add-on monitoring
crm-s › components › access › buildBuy › summary: Built from CRM sharing and restriction rules. Event monitoring in the security add-on reports access to the province's security team.
crm-s › components › access › watch › text: Staff with full access, and programs running with full rights, can get past the restrictions. Keeping service lines apart depends on keeping those rights from people.
crm-s › components › notices › name: Notices and documents
crm-s › components › notices › short: Letters, forms and court papers
crm-s › components › notices › what: Templates for the notices, forms and court documents the ministry sends. Children's services alone need about 150.
crm-s › components › notices › does: It fills in templates from case data and stores the PDF that was sent as the official copy.
crm-s › components › notices › why: Clients have a right to clear written decisions. The stored copy proves what was sent and when.
crm-s › components › notices › buildBuy › label: Platform: document generation tool, part of the public sector package
crm-s › components › notices › buildBuy › summary: Document generation comes with the public sector package. The CRM provider sells no e-signature product, so signing needs a separate product. DocuSign is already used with the ministry's CRM contract system.
crm-s › components › notices › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Document generation tool

crm-s › components › notices › watch › text: If legal advice requires a digital certificate signature on some documents, no CRM product can do it. A separate product such as DocuSign would be needed.
crm-s › components › payments › name: Payments and debt
crm-s › components › payments › short: Monthly payments and overpayments
crm-s › components › payments › what: The monthly payment run and the records of what each client is owed and owes, built inside the CRM platform.
crm-s › components › payments › does: It runs the monthly payments and sends cheque and direct deposit files to the bank, the mail service and the province's accounting system. It keeps debt records like the mainframe does today.
crm-s › components › payments › why: Clients rely on being paid on time every month. Errors here cost money and cause real hardship.
crm-s › components › payments › buildBuy › label: Build on the CRM platform
crm-s › components › payments › buildBuy › summary: The CRM platform has no benefit ledger. Its billing and loan collection products were judged a poor fit for public sector overpayment rules. So the payment run and debt records are custom work.
crm-s › components › payments › watch › text: The CRM provider sets its own upgrade dates three times a year. The ministry cannot stop an upgrade during the monthly cheque run, which it can do today.
crm-s › components › platform-services › name: Platform services
crm-s › components › platform-services › short: Security, privacy, backup and reports
crm-s › components › platform-services › what: CRM add-ons that every part of the system uses: encryption and access monitoring, privacy tools, test data masking, backup, dashboards and release tools.
crm-s › components › platform-services › does: They protect data, keep history, apply retention rules, back up records and show managers how work is going.
crm-s › components › platform-services › why: Records about children must be kept up to 90 years and others for shorter periods. These tools make keeping and destroying records on schedule possible.
crm-s › components › platform-services › buildBuy › label: Buy: several CRM add-ons
crm-s › components › platform-services › buildBuy › summary: The security add-on is priced as a share of spend. The privacy, test data masking and backup add-ons, extra storage and test environments are each separate add-ons. Each analytics tool is priced per user. None of these is in the staff licence price.
crm-s › components › platform-services › buildBuy › options › 1 › name: Security add-on

crm-s › components › platform-services › buildBuy › options › 3 › note: Priced by storage
crm-s › components › platform-services › buildBuy › options › 4 › name: Analytics tools
crm-s › components › platform-services › buildBuy › options › 4 › note: Dashboards and reports
crm-s › components › platform-services › watch › text: The CRM provider does not say how much recent data could be lost in an outage. It is also unknown whether a record can be fully removed from the CRM provider's backups when the law requires it.
crm-s › components › integration-hub › name: Integration hub
crm-s › components › integration-hub › short: Connects to outside organizations
crm-s › components › integration-hub › what: The integration platform, the CRM provider's product for connecting systems, running on ministry servers.
crm-s › components › integration-hub › does: It passes data to and from banks, the mail service, the accounting system, Canada Revenue Agency, Service Canada, courts, police and others. It sends some data in files on a schedule.
crm-s › components › integration-hub › why: Payments, identity checks and court work all depend on these links. Running it on CSBC servers keeps it under the ministry's control.
crm-s › components › integration-hub › buildBuy › label: Buy: the CRM provider's integration platform, priced by capacity
crm-s › components › integration-hub › buildBuy › summary: The integration platform is sold separately from the CRM licence. It runs on the ministry's own servers, so it is not affected by CRM maintenance. Building the connections is about 1,140 person-days.
crm-s › components › integration-hub › watch › text: The CRM platform keeps change messages for only 72 hours. A long weekend outage could lose some. That is still better than today.
crm-s › components › siebel-connector › name: Siebel connector
crm-s › components › siebel-connector › short: Links old and new during the switch
crm-s › components › siebel-connector › what: A connector on the integration platform that lets the CRM platform and Siebel share data while both are running.
crm-s › components › siebel-connector › does: It keeps cases in step between the two systems while work moves over in stages.
crm-s › components › siebel-connector › why: Programs will move one at a time. Staff and clients must not lose information in between. This work is about 930 person-days.
crm-s › components › siebel-connector › buildBuy › label: Buy: an integration platform connector for Oracle Siebel
crm-s › components › siebel-connector › buildBuy › summary: This is a premium connector, bought on top of the integration platform itself.
crm-s › components › finance › name: Finance partners
crm-s › components › finance › short: Bank, mail service, accounting
crm-s › components › finance › what: The bank, BC Mail Plus, the province's corporate accounting system and the Treasury.
crm-s › components › finance › does: They receive payment files, print and mail cheques and notices, and record the money in the province's books.
crm-s › components › finance › why: Every client payment passes through them. The links must work on time every month.
crm-s › components › government › name: Government and justice partners
crm-s › components › government › short: Other governments, courts, health

crm-s › components › government › does: They share information used to check eligibility, run court steps and provide health benefits.
crm-s › components › government › why: Correct, timely information from partners prevents wrong payments and supports child safety work.
crm-s › components › reporting-store › name: Reporting store
crm-s › components › reporting-store › short: Reports for managers and planners

crm-s › components › reporting-store › does: Managers and analysts use it for reports and planning without slowing the main system.

crm-s › components › reporting-store › buildBuy › options › 2 › note: Can also run on CSBC servers
crm-s › components › reporting-store › watch › text: Reports work from a copy made each night, as they do today. The goal of reporting without making copies of personal data is not met.
crm-s › components › continuity-store › name: Continuity store
crm-s › components › continuity-store › short: Backup copy of records, no functions
crm-s › components › continuity-store › what: A copy of the system's records on CSBC servers, kept up to date by a steady feed of changes from the CRM platform.
crm-s › components › continuity-store › does: It holds the records so staff can still look up cases and drive emergency payments if the CRM platform is unavailable.
crm-s › components › continuity-store › why: Without it, a supplier cut-off would leave staff with no case information and clients with no payments.
crm-s › components › continuity-store › buildBuy › label: Build on CSBC servers, fed from the CRM platform
crm-s › components › continuity-store › buildBuy › summary: The feed uses the CRM platform's change data capture, a paid add-on. The CRM backup add-on adds a second copy.

crm-s › components › continuity-store › buildBuy › options › 1 › note: Paid by usage
crm-s › components › continuity-store › watch › text: The copy holds records only. No CRM rules or screens can run outside the CRM platform, so the system itself cannot keep working if the CRM provider cuts off access. Siebel never faced this risk.
crm-s › components › manual-payment › name: Manual payment procedure
crm-s › components › manual-payment › short: Emergency payments by hand
crm-s › components › manual-payment › what: The written plan for paying clients by hand if the CRM platform is cut off. It carries over today's business continuity plan.
crm-s › components › manual-payment › does: Staff use the continuity copy to make payments manually until service returns.
crm-s › components › manual-payment › why: People must still be paid if the system is down. A plan that is rehearsed works better in a crisis.
